diagnosis: Either: Counts the starting number as the first count rather than counting the jumps back. Or: Counts back only 2 instead of 3.
rationale: The learner said '12, 11, 10' for 12 - 3, including 12 in their 3-count instead of hopping back 3 units to reach 9. A number line demonstrating counting back with visible hops clearly shows that the first hop lands on 11, not 12.

script.focus: Notice that the first hop back lands on 13, not 14.

intent: Demonstrate subtract on the number-line with values [14,4]. Tutor points at: Notice that the first hop back lands on 13, not 14.

content.title: Counting back, one hop at a time

frames.caption: Start at 14. We are standing here; we have not hopped yet.
Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started.

judgement.reasoning: The demonstration explicitly addresses the exact misconception ('Start at 14. We are standing here; we have not hopped yet. Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started.'). It uses a worked demo representation (passive visual walkthrough rather than interactive plotting), simplifies cognitive load, stays well within grade-1 scope, and does not leak the answer to the active problem (12 - 3).
judgement.verdict: A teacher would definitely use this clear, targeted worked example to clarify that the first hop lands on the next number.
